newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Globus expects to post 1996/97 loss.
newsitem.headline: Globus expects to post 1996/97 loss.

text.p: Swiss retail chain Magazine zum Globus said it expected to post a double-digit million Swiss franc loss in the business year ending on February 28, 1997.

"We will have a double-digit (million) negative net income," finance director Rudolf Wenger told Reuters after the company said in a statement it would post an operational loss and incur significant one-off costs as well.
"The board and management expect a negative operational result for the current business year," it said.

"In addition, one-off, extraordinary costs and reserves in significant magnitude will be incurred for integrating six Jelmoli stores, for splitting with ABM Austria, for repositioning Globus and ABM in Switzerland and for revaluing inventory," it said without giving any figures.
Globus last year posted a group profit of 4.5 million francs, down from 35.8 million the year before.
Globus last year bought six stores from rival department store Jelmoli and said their integration into the Globus network as of August 1 was going according to plan.
"Starting with the 1997/98 business year, Globus stores will generate two-thirds more turnover," it added.

As of August 31, half way through the current business year, Globus group sales were up 1.8 percent adjusted for currency fluctuations, it said. Sales in Switzerland slipped 0.3 percent despite the addition of the new Jelmoli stores.
Unadjusted foreign sales rose 15.1 percent, but it gave no absolute figures.
